mechanism_narrative: When the Federal Funds Rate remains persistently below its pre-pandemic median for at least 3 consecutive months, it reduces the real discount rate applied to future earnings, thereby boosting equity valuations and driving positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: Over a 60-day window following the trigger, SPX 20-day forward returns are not statistically different from the 30-day moving average of the prior 60-day period (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in monthly employment growth (PAYEMS) accompanied by a simultaneous decline in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) signals a strengthening labor market, which raises consumer confidence and corporate earnings expectations, producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS crosses above its 5-week moving average while UNRATE falls below its 5-week moving average
failure_condition: In the 20-day window after the trigger, SPX 20-day forward returns are negative and the 95% confidence interval does not include the mean of the prior 20-day returns (p-value < 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly expansion in industrial production (INDPRO) above trend, persisting for at least two consecutive months, reflects robust economic momentum that reduces growth uncertainty and supports higher equity valuations, yielding positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: Over the 5-day horizon, the 20-day forward return is less than the 5-day average of the prior 20-day forward returns (t-test p < 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When consumer price inflation (CPIAUCSL) unexpectedly rises by more than 0.3 percentage points in a single month, it prompts the Federal Reserve to signal tighter policy, which compresses growth expectations and can produce negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: In the 20-day window following the inflation surprise, the SPX 20-day forward return is positive and statistically significant (p < 0.05) compared to the prior 20-day average return.

mechanism_narrative: Consecutive months of declining residential housing starts (HOUST) indicate cooling real estate activity, which raises financing costs and reduces corporate investment, thereby generating negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: Over the 60-day window after the trigger, SPX 20-day forward returns are not statistically different from the prior 60-day average (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sudden drop in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) below 4.0% combined with a decline in labor force participation (PAYEMS) suggests a tight labor market that can fuel wage growth and inflationary pressures, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns remain positive and statistically significant (p < 0.05) during the 20-day window after the trigger.

mechanism_narrative: A double-dip contraction in industrial production (INDPRO) in two consecutive months signals supply-side weakness and heightened uncertainty, which can depress equity valuations and produce negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO falls for two consecutive months
failure_condition: The 5-day SPX 20-day forward return is higher than the 5-day average of the prior 20-day forward returns (p < 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When the 3-month moving average of RSAFS (reserves) exceeds 4.5 billion dollars for three consecutive months, it indicates aggressive balance sheet expansion by banks, lowering funding costs and supporting equity valuations, which tends to produce positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days in a post-QE normalization regime.
candidate_trigger: 3-month moving average of RSAFS > 4.5B for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns in the 20-day window after the trigger are not statistically different from the prior 20-day average (p > 0.05).
